items.title: 18.2.1 Limitations to the Law of Independent Assortment

blocks.text: The law of independent assortment explains how many genes are inherited, but it does not cover every genetic complexity.

items: Linked genes: genes close together on the same chromosome are often inherited together, not independently (gene linkage).
Chromosome crossover: the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes in meiosis, so the ratios of gene combinations may differ from the prediction.
Epistasis: the effect of one gene is modified or suppressed by one or more unrelated genes, which also changes the expected ratios.
Pleiotropy: one gene controls several characters, so those characters behave as linked and can distort the expected ratios.
Environmental effect: many phenotypes are affected by the environment.
